newsitem.title: USA: NYS credit ratings hurt by lack of a budget-McCall.
newsitem.headline: NYS credit ratings hurt by lack of a budget-McCall.

text.p: The New York State comptroller on Tuesday said that the state's failure to approve a budget was hurting its finances as well as its credit rating.
"The dysfunctional budget process only reinforces Wall Street's dim view of New York's finances and keeps our credit ratings at the bottom of the list," McCall said, in prepared remarks.
The state's budget was due on April 1, but it, along with a host of other bills, was delayed by the feud over apartment rent rules that was resolved early Monday morning.

Gov George Pataki, who spoke to reporters on Monday after reaching a preliminary pact on the controversial apartment rent rules, said that he expected to submit a bill for a one-week interim budget, as the present pact ends on June 20. He added that he did not anticipate the one-week extension to contain any controversial items.
The Republican governor, who also has to work out an accord for a new welfare plan by July 1, a federal deadline, said he thought it was possible to meet that date but added this would be diffciult.

The state comptroller, a potential Democrate candidate for governor in next year's election, said that the state's failure to again approve a budget on time, a long-running pattern, interferred with planning by lawmakers as well as taxpayers through-out the state, which must set school budgets without knowing how much aid they will get from Albany.
He added the number of issues put on hold includes legislation to aid distressed local governments.
